ED Attendance report: site_name

2024-09-02

Abstract

This study is aimed at identifying large changes in presentations over time across different sites, to identify where we have the most statistically different increases. In addition a cohort of patients is identified that could potentially benefit from non ED services.

This is an analysis of ED attendances across the SW region, focusing on the 5 most common, non ambulance conveyances to type 1 departments. The data has been analysed using XXX methodology to identify avoidanble attendances. A sub group of patients who are not classified as avoidable attendances or subsequently become admissions has been identified, these are patients who are currently appropriate for ED but only have minor investigations and procedures before discharge. We have analysed the demographics of these patients for personal characteristics as well as their attendance patterns to help identify a patient group that an alternative provision outside of ED could be developed.

Method

Data was taken from ECDS for the last 18 months of non ambulance conveyances. The top 5 presentations per site were identified by number of attendances using SNOMED codes. The dataset was filtered to remove admitted patients. Avoidable attendances were identified useing XXX methodology. The data was further analysed to create a cohort of patients who were of minor acuity and recieved low level investigations and treatments.

This cohort was then further analyised to identify characteristics of these patients using cluster analysis to try to identify key groups of patients. This included demographic, geographic and time attendance patterns.

A resource time was created by removing the wait time from the total time in department to give a proxy for resource utilisation time in department.

This report utilises an avoidable attendances methodology to help identify a middle ground of patients. These are a cohort of patients who are non ambulance conveyances to a type 1

Benchmarking change over time

These charts look at the last 6 months of attendances and compare them to the same 6 months a year ago. The percentage change is then calculated. This is broken down across the various attendance types we have identified.

We are most interested in this study for the change in divertible attendances.The other types are provided for context. Further in the report we can see this in a more traditional time series for this individual site.

Guide for interpreting the box plot:

Key Components of a Box Plot:

Box: The central rectangle represents the interquartile range (IQR), which contains the middle 50% of the data.

Median: The line within the box indicates the median value, separating the lower and upper halves of the data.

Whiskers: The lines extending from the box are called whiskers. They typically reach to the minimum and maximum values excluding outliers.

Outliers: Data points that fall outside of the whiskers, represented by the dots, are considered outliers.
